stem:
The diagram shows Reyansh's brass strip. A flame heats the left end. Drawing pins W, X, Y and Z are stuck with wax along the strip, with W nearest the flame and Z farthest.

Which claim about heat transfer along the strip is correct?

options.text: Heat moves by conduction from the hot end toward colder parts, so the pins fall in the order W, then X, then Y, then Z.
Heat moves by conduction from the cold end toward the flame, so the pins fall in the order Z, then Y, then X, then W.
All four pins fall at the same instant because brass is one solid piece.
Only pin W can fall, because heat never leaves the flame end of a solid strip.

teacher.key_rationale: In conduction, heat travels from the heated end along the strip, so wax nearest the flame melts first.
teacher.figure_note: rewritten brass strip with pins W–Z
